Baoguo Temple Main Hall

Baoguo Si Dadian

Built: 1013 Dynasty: Song Dynasty Location: Ningbo, Zhejiang Admission: 20 CNY Time needed: 1-2 hrs

Honest note: Only the Main Hall is Song. Other temple halls are later additions.

Basis: 1961 NPU — click Authenticity Labels to understand our classification system.

Why Visit

Oldest wooden structure in southern China, built 1013. Masterpiece of Song timber framing that predates the official Song building manual (Yingzao Fashi, 1103).

How to Get There

Baoguo Temple (保国寺) is 15km north of Ningbo city center in Hongtang Town (洪塘镇). Fly into Ningbo Lishe Airport (NGB, 15km south of city) or fly into Shanghai (PVG/SHA) and take HSR. From Shanghai: HSR from Shanghai Hongqiao to Ningbo (2 hours, 140 CNY, departures every 30 min). From Hangzhou: HSR to Ningbo (1 hour, 80 CNY). From Ningbo Railway Station: Bus 238 to Baoguo Temple stop (40 min, 2 CNY). Taxi from Ningbo city center/Tianyi Square: 30 min (50 CNY). The temple entrance is on a hillside -- a short uphill walk from the bus stop. Ningbo Metro Line 2 to Lucheng Station, then taxi 10 min (15 CNY).

Where to Stay

Stay in Ningbo city center -- the temple area is suburban with no nearby hotels. Ningbo Marriott Hotel (600 CNY/night, riverfront Old Bund location, best upscale); Crowne Plaza City Center (500 CNY/night, near Tianyi Square shopping area); Home Inn Ningbo Railway Station (180 CNY/night, reliable budget chain). For a local experience: Flower Blooms Boutique Hotel near Moon Lake (350 CNY/night, converted traditional house). Old Bund (Laowaitan) area is the nicest place to stay -- riverside promenade with bars and restaurants.

What to Eat

Ningbo cuisine (宁波菜) is one of China's great regional cooking styles, focused on fresh seafood and delicate flavors. Must-try: Ningbo tang yuan (宁波汤圆, glutinous rice balls filled with black sesame paste in sweet osmanthus soup, 15-25 CNY -- best at Gang Ya Gou 缸鸭狗 near Tianyi Square, a famous shop since 1926); yellow croaker in soy sauce (雪菜大黄鱼, Ningbo's signature fish dish, 60-100 CNY at seafood restaurants); xie chao nian gao (蟹炒年糕, wok-fried rice cakes with crab, 40-60 CNY). The Old Bund (Laowaitan, 老外滩) riverside has dozens of restaurants -- Chamate (慈舍) serves elegant Ningbo cuisine in a heritage building (100-150 CNY/person). Near the temple: Hongtang town has simple noodle shops serving Ningbo-style seafood noodles (15-25 CNY).

Best Time to Visit

Spring (March-May): 12-25C, cherry blossoms in the temple courtyard (late March), best season. Autumn (October-November): 15-22C, clear skies, persimmons ripen on temple trees. Avoid mid-June to early July -- the Meiyu (plum rain) season brings 3-4 weeks of continuous rain and 85%+ humidity, very uncomfortable. Summer (July-August): 28-38C, humid, visitable but sweaty. Winter (December-February): 5-10C, damp cold. The temple is rarely crowded in any season -- it is overlooked by domestic tourists who focus on Tianyi Pavilion and the Bund. Hours: 8am-4:30pm. Admission: 20 CNY.

Tips for Foreign Travelers

Only the Main Hall (Dadian) is Song dynasty (1013) -- it is the oldest surviving wooden building in southern China. Other halls in the complex are Ming-Qing reconstructions. The Main Hall's dougong (斗拱) bracket system predates the official Song building code Yingzao Fashi (营造法式, 1103) -- this makes it the earliest datable example of mature Chinese timber-frame architecture. The temple is virtually unknown to foreign tourists -- you will likely be alone here, which is a rare luxury at a national treasure site in China. The temple caretakers may offer to show you hidden details (Buddhist carvings on ceiling beams) for a small tip. After the temple: combine with Tianyi Pavilion (天一阁, 30 min by taxi, China's oldest private library from 1561, 30 CNY) and Ningbo Museum (宁波博物馆, designed by Pritzker winner Wang Shu, free, stunning building made of recycled bricks and tiles -- 20 min by taxi).
